newsitem.title: USA: Ford hopes for UAW agreement Monday.
newsitem.headline: Ford hopes for UAW agreement Monday.

text.p: Ford Motor Co chairman Alex Trotman said Monday he hopes the company will reach a tentative agreement later Monday for a new national labor contract with the United Auto Workers Union.
Trotman told a news conference here that the tone of the negotiations is "positive and constructive."
"I don't really know when they'll be finished. I hope they'll be finished today, but I don't know that," Trotman told reporters before a speech to the Detroit Economic Club.
He said there are a number of issues that have yet to be resolved but said that there was no single sticking point in the talks.
He said the company and the union have discussed several possible contract lengths longer than three years, but he declined to elaborate.
Ford has previously said that it would like an agreement longer than the traditional three year UAW contract because it would allow the automaker to stabilize its costs over a longer period.

Trotman added that the company needed to maintain a balance in the contract between meeting the union's needs and improving its own efficiency. "One of our key objectives as manufacturers is to maintain as much flexibility and competitiveness as we possibly can," Trotman said.

He said Ford's bargaining teams are continuing to communicate with their counterparts at General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp, but he declined to say how a Ford-UAW agreement would affect those competitors.
